quickAnswer: To calculate SIP maturity value, use: M = P × [(1 + r)ⁿ − 1] ÷ r × (1 + r), where P is the monthly instalment, r is the monthly rate (annual rate ÷ 12), and n is the total number of instalments. With a ₹5,000 monthly SIP at 12% annual return over 10 years, the maturity value is approximately ₹11.6 lakh on ₹6 lakh invested.

howto.name: How to Calculate SIP Mutual Fund Returns
howto.description: Step-by-step instructions for modeling monthly investments, annual compounding returns, and annual step-up contributions.

steps.name: Enter Monthly Investment Amount
steps.text: Input the fixed dollar amount you intend to invest every month into your mutual fund or ETF portfolio.

steps.name: Specify Expected Annual Return Rate
steps.text: Enter your estimated long-term annualized rate of return (e.g. 8%, noting that returns are assumptions).

steps.name: Set Investment Time Horizon
steps.text: Specify the number of years you plan to remain continuously invested.

steps.name: Add Optional Annual Step-Up Percentage
steps.text: Optionally model annual salary increases by stepping up your monthly contributions by 5% or 10% each year.

steps.name: Analyze Wealth Accumulation
steps.text: Review total principal invested, estimated compound wealth gains, final portfolio value, and the annual growth breakdown.

faqs.q: What is a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP)?
faqs.a: A Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) is an investment vehicle that allows individuals to contribute a fixed dollar amount into a mutual fund, ETF, or index portfolio at regular monthly intervals, taking advantage of rupee/dollar cost averaging and compounding returns.

faqs.q: Are the returns projected by this SIP calculator guaranteed?
faqs.a: No. The returns displayed are mathematical projections based strictly on your assumed annual return rate. Mutual funds and stock market securities carry market risk and returns fluctuate continuously.

faqs.q: What is an annual Step-Up SIP?
faqs.a: A Step-Up (or Top-Up) SIP automatically increases your monthly installment amount by a fixed percentage (e.g., 10%) once every 12 months. This mirrors annual career salary raises and substantially accelerates long-term wealth compounding.

faqs.q: What is the formula for calculating SIP returns?
faqs.a: The standard monthly compounding formula is: M = P × [((1 + i)^n - 1) / i] × (1 + i), where P is the periodic monthly investment, i is the periodic monthly interest rate (annual rate ÷ 1200), and n is the total number of monthly contributions. The SIP calculator uses the nominal annual rate divided by 12 as the monthly rate, so results can differ slightly from calculators that use an effective monthly rate.

faqs.q: Is my investment plan or financial data uploaded to any server?
faqs.a: No. All SIP calculations execute 100% locally in your web browser. No portfolio amounts or private financial plans are ever uploaded or tracked.
